extraction.name: EuroSAT
extraction.description: A novel satellite image dataset for land use and land cover classification based on Sentinel-2 satellite images. The dataset consists of 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images with 10 different classes, covering 13 spectral bands in the visible, near infrared and short wave infrared part of the spectrum.
extraction.creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
extraction.publisher: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Satellite images from Sentinel-2A were downloaded via Amazon S3, covering European cities from the European Urban Atlas across 34 countries. Images with low cloud levels were selected, recorded throughout the year to capture high variance. 27,000 georeferenced image patches (64x64 pixels) were manually checked and labeled into 10 land use/land cover classes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral satellite imagery from Sentinel-2A covering 13 spectral bands with spatial resolutions of 10-60 meters per pixel. The raw data consists of satellite images of European cities with associated cloud level metadata provided by ESA.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Images recorded throughout the year from Sentinel-2A satellite launched in June 2015
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Image patches were manually checked after extraction from satellite images. Patches were extracted based on European Urban Atlas cities and labeled according to 10 land use and land cover classes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The classification system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow a finely graduated per-pixel segmentation
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables applications in agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change, urban development, environmental monitoring, deforestation detection, nature protection, and sustainable development. It can assist in detecting illegal clearing of forests and monitoring urban area development.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training deep neural networks for satellite image classification, land use and land cover change detection, monitoring Earth's land surfaces, improving geographical maps, detecting deforestation, urban development monitoring
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were selected to cover high intra-class variance by extracting images from multiple countries (34 European countries) and recorded throughout the year. Images were selected with low cloud levels to improve quality.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Satellite images were filtered by cloud level using ESA-provided cloud level values. Images were extracted as 64x64 pixel patches and manually checked. Images were georeferenced and labeled into 10 classes.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: While a classiﬁcation system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow a ﬁnely graduated per-pixel segmentation, it cannot only detect changes as shown in the previous examples, it can also facilitate keeping maps up-to-date.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: applications in the domains of agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change, urban development, or environmental monitoring can be realized... The presented examples are particularly of interest in urban area development, nature protection or sustainable development. For instance, deforestation is a main contributor to climate change, therefore the detection of deforested land is of particular interest (e.g., to notice illegal clearing of forests).

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We provide this work in the context of the recently published EuroSAT dataset, which can be used similar to [18] as a basis for a large-scale training of deep neural networks for the task of satellite image classiﬁcation... This work is a ﬁrst important step to make use of the large amount of available satellite data in machine learning allowing to monitor Earth's land surfaces on a large scale. The proposed dataset can be leveraged for multiple real-world Earth observation applications. Possible applications are land use and land cover change detection or the improvement of geographical maps.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We aimed for the objective to cover as many countries as possible in the EuroSAT dataset in order to cover the high intra-class variance inherent to remotely sensed images. Furthermore, we have extracted images recorded all over the year to get a variance as high as possible inherent in the covered land use and land cover classes.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: In order to improve the chance of getting valuable image patches, we selected satellite images with a low cloud level. Besides the possibility to generate a cloud mask, ESA provides a cloud level value for each satellite image allowing to quickly select images with a low percentage of clouds covering the land scene... we created a dataset of 27,000 georeferenced and labeled image patches. The image patches measure 64x64 pixels and have been manually checked.
